chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) recited: 'And the beautiful word of your Lord has been accomplished truly and justly.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, we only recite it as: And the word of your Lord has been accomplished truly and justly.' So he said: 'Surely, in it is 'the beautiful'.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'Al-Husna' in Surah Al-An'am according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq (as) confirming the inclusion of 'al-Husna' (the Beautiful) in the phrase 'Kallimat Rabbika' based on the Shia recension of the Quran, contrasting it with the common Uthmani recitation. It serves as a key textual evidence for the Shia doctrine of Quranic preservation, asserting that the complete divine wording includes specific epithets often omitted in mainstream Sunni recensions. This distinction underscores the Shia view that the Quran's text remains intact and unaltered, preserving all nuances of divine attributes.
